content: Induration, in the context of pathology, refers to the hardening of a specific area of the body. This hardening can occur as a reaction to inflammation, increased blood flow (hyperemia), or the infiltration of neoplastic cells. Additionally, the term can describe a region or part of the body that has undergone such a process of hardening. The term induration is most commonly used in dermatological findings to describe changes in the skin or subcutaneous tissue. For example, in the context of tuberculin sensitivity tests, both erythema (redness) and induration are considered reliable indicators of a positive reaction. In one case, erythema was observed to have spread to 20 cm, while the central area of induration extended to 9 cm. These findings are supported by references such as the Random House Webster's Unabridged Dictionary and studies like Kimura et al.'s comparison of erythema and induration in tuberculin tests, as well as Race et al.'s documentation of a painful nodule with induration and spreading erythema.
